title: Review of c11's active-nematic 1.5x-resolution finding: seed 4 reproduces a single-founder colony by fission (1 -> 14 rods, generation 4, 0 merges); seed 3 never nucleates at the finer grid (Supported, with nucleation not robust)
summary: Looked at fission_strips_res15.png and the finding's sheet, then ran the colony world at 1.5x resolution (WORLD_P dx=0.6667, --size 192 192, same physical domain, T=1000) on fresh seeds 3 and 4. Seed 4: one droplet nucleates at t~135, becomes a rod with a vortex pair by t~175, divides by elongation and a central pinch, and its line grows and branches into 14 separate rods by t=1000 (rerun_res15/seed4/sheet.png): 12 splits, 7 persistent, max generation 4, 0 merges, 11 long-lived tracks >= 1 body length (max 2.8). Seed 3: the noise relaxes to the uniform state and no droplet ever nucleates (0 bodies to t=1000, rerun_res15/seed3/sheet.png). So when a nucleus forms, the rod body plan and binary fission survive the finer grid as the finding says, but at 1.5x resolution nucleation from noise becomes rare enough to fail on one of two seeds: S at the finer grid is seed-dependent.

observations.D: numbers.txt and rerun_res15/seed4/sheet.png: 1 founder -> 14 rods, 7 persistent splits, generation 4, 0 merges at dx 2/3

controls_run.D: the finding is itself a resolution control of 20261025T1014-c11-active-nematic-colony; my dx=1 runs of that world on seeds 3 and 4 (review 20261025T1125-c03-review-nematic-colony) gave 25 persistent splits each

verdicts.limitation: Nucleation at the finer grid failed on seed 3, so the colony's appearance from noise is not resolution-robust; the per-cell noise amplitude is fixed, so the noise is weaker per unit area at finer dx, which may explain it.
